34545.q: Which list has Bern's old town been on since 1983?
34545.e: Bern's old town has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983. It is considered a particularly well-preserved medieval town.
34545.m: Bern's old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

34546.q: What are the long, covered walkways in Bern's old town called?
34546.e: The arcades are covered passages under the houses. You can shop there and stay dry even when it rains.
34546.m: In Bern you can walk under the arcades and stay dry.

34547.q: Who meets in the Parliament Building of the Federal Palace in Bern?
a: The National Council and the Council of States
34547.e: The chambers of the National Council and the Council of States are in the Parliament Building. They discuss laws there during the sessions.
34547.m: The National Council and the Council of States meet in the Parliament Building.

34548.q: How many parts does the Federal Palace have?
34548.e: The Federal Palace is made up of the Federal Palace West, the Parliament Building in the middle and the Federal Palace East.
34548.m: The Federal Palace has three parts.

34549.q: Which part of the Federal Palace is the oldest?
34549.e: The Federal Palace West was built as early as 1852 to 1857. The Federal Palace East and the Parliament Building were added later.
34549.m: The Federal Palace West is the oldest part.

34550.q: Which group of stone figures stands in the great hall under the dome of the Federal Palace?
34550.e: The big stone sculpture shows the three Confederates swearing the Rütli Oath. It was unveiled in 1914.
34550.m: A big stone sculpture of the three Confederates stands in the Federal Palace.

34551.q: Which stone are the outside walls of the Federal Palace mainly built from?
34551.e: The outside walls are made of Bernese sandstone. Many houses in the old town are made of this stone too.
34551.m: The Federal Palace is built of sandstone.

34552.q: Where do the many different stones in the Parliament Building come from?
34552.e: About 30 kinds of stone from 13 cantons were used in the Parliament Building. That way the whole country is meant to be represented in the building.
34552.m: The Federal Palace contains stones from many parts of Switzerland.

34553.q: What is the big square right in front of the Federal Palace called?
34553.e: The Bundesplatz is on the north side of the Parliament Building. Markets and festivals are often held there.
34553.m: The Bundesplatz lies in front of the Federal Palace.

34554.q: What takes place on the Bundesplatz on Tuesdays and Saturdays?
34554.e: On Tuesdays and Saturdays there is a weekly market on the Bundesplatz and in the streets next to it. You can buy vegetables, fruit and cheese.
34554.m: There is a market on the Bundesplatz twice a week.

34555.q: Which bank has its seat right on the Bundesplatz in Bern?
34555.e: The Swiss National Bank has a building on the Bundesplatz. It looks after Switzerland's money.
34555.m: The National Bank stands on the Bundesplatz in Bern.

34556.q: What is shown with light on the front of the Federal Palace on the Bundesplatz on autumn evenings?
34556.e: At the “Rendez-vous Bundesplatz” in autumn, a light and sound show is projected onto the Federal Palace. Lots of families watch.
34556.m: In autumn a light show glows on the Federal Palace at the Bundesplatz.

34557.q: Which cantonal bank also stands on the Bundesplatz?
34557.e: The Bernese Cantonal Bank has its head office on the west side of the Bundesplatz. After all, the square is in Bern.
34557.m: The Bernese Cantonal Bank also stands on the Bundesplatz.

34558.q: What can be seen in the middle of the glass dome inside?
34558.e: In the middle of the glass dome there is the Swiss coat of arms as a mosaic. It is surrounded by oak leaves.
34558.m: The Swiss coat of arms is in the middle of the dome.

34559.q: Which coats of arms can be seen around the Swiss coat of arms in the glass dome?
a: the coats of arms of the cantons
the coats of arms of the neighbouring countries
the coats of arms of the Federal Councillors
the coats of arms of Europe's cities
34559.e: The coats of arms of the cantons are painted on glass around the Swiss coat of arms. They stand for the cantons that together make up Switzerland.
34559.m: The coats of arms of the cantons shine in the dome.

34560.q: Which saying is written in the dome of the Federal Palace?
a: One for all, all for one
34560.e: The dome says in Latin “Unus pro omnibus, omnes pro uno”. That means “One for all, all for one”.
34560.m: “One for all, all for one” is written in the dome.

34562.q: Which animal is on the coat of arms of Bern, the city with the Federal Palace?
34562.e: The Bern coat of arms shows a bear. That is why you find lots of bears in Bern and in the Federal Palace.
34562.m: The animal on Bern's coat of arms is the bear.

34563.q: How much does a public tour of the Federal Palace cost?
34563.e: Tours of the Federal Palace are free. Very many visitors come every year.
34563.m: A tour of the Federal Palace is free.

34564.q: Roughly how long does a public tour of the Federal Palace last?
34564.e: A public tour lasts about an hour. You see the most important rooms.
34564.m: A tour of the Federal Palace lasts about an hour.

34565.q: What do you have to go through at the entrance of the Federal Palace before a tour?
34565.e: At the entrance there is a security check like at an airport. Bags are X-rayed.
34565.m: There is a security check before visiting the Federal Palace.

34566.q: Roughly how many people visit the Federal Palace each year?
34566.e: According to Parliament, over 100,000 people visit the Federal Palace every year. Many of them are school classes.
34566.m: Over 100,000 people visit the Federal Palace every year.

34567.q: During a session, where can visitors watch the politicians from?
34567.e: The council chambers have public galleries. From there you can follow the debates.
34567.m: You can watch Parliament from the public gallery.

34568.q: What do visitors aged 16 and over have to show at the entrance of the Federal Palace?
34568.e: Anyone over 16 has to show the security staff an official ID with a photo, for example an identity card.
34568.m: From the age of 16 you need an ID to visit the Federal Palace.

34569.q: On which river is the Bear Park in Bern?
34569.e: The Bear Park is on the bank of the Aare, opposite the old town. The bears can even go into the water.
34569.m: Bern's Bear Park is on the Aare.

34570.q: Why does the city of Bern keep bears at the Bear Park?
a: The bear is the animal on Bern's coat of arms
34570.e: The bear is on the coat of arms of the city and canton of Bern. That is why Bern has kept live bears for centuries.
34570.m: The bear is the animal on Bern's coat of arms.

34572.q: Why was a big Bear Park built next to the old bear pit?
a: so the bears have more space
34572.e: In the old round pit the bears did not have enough space. The Bear Park is much bigger and more natural.
34572.m: In the Bear Park the bears have more space than in the old pit.

34573.q: What do the bears in the Bear Park often do in winter?
a: They eat especially much every day
They swim in the Aare every day
34573.e: Brown bears have a winter rest. They then sleep a lot in their den.
34573.m: In winter bears have a winter rest.

34574.q: According to legend, which animal was Bern named after?
34574.e: According to legend, the town was to be named after the first animal killed in a hunt. That was a bear (Bär in German).
34574.m: According to legend, Bern got its name from a bear.

34575.q: Which zoo does the Bear Park in Bern belong to?
34575.e: The Bear Park is part of Bern Animal Park. The main site of this animal park is called Dählhölzli.
34575.m: The Bear Park belongs to the Dählhölzli Animal Park.

34576.q: What are the three levels of the state in Switzerland called?
34576.e: In Switzerland the Confederation, the cantons and the municipalities share the tasks. This is called federalism.
34576.m: In Switzerland the Confederation, cantons and municipalities share the work.

34577.q: Who is responsible for the army in Switzerland?
34577.e: National defence is a task of the Confederation. That is why there is a single Swiss army.
34577.m: The Confederation is responsible for the army.

34578.q: Who looks after Switzerland's relations with other countries?
34578.e: Foreign policy is a task of the Confederation. It makes treaties with other states.
34578.m: The Confederation looks after relations with other countries.

34579.q: Who decides what road signs look like all over Switzerland?
34579.e: The rules for road signs are made by the Confederation. That is why a stop sign in Geneva looks the same as one in St Gallen.
34579.m: The Confederation decides what road signs look like.

34580.q: What is the Swiss army called because most soldiers have another job?
34580.e: Most members of the army only serve for a few weeks a year. The rest of the time they work in their normal job.
34580.m: The Swiss army is a militia army.

34581.q: What is the first training for young soldiers in Switzerland called?
34581.e: In recruit school, RS for short, young soldiers learn the basics. It lasts several months.
34581.m: Young soldiers start with recruit school.

34582.q: Which famous knife is part of the Swiss soldiers' equipment?
34582.e: Swiss soldiers get a pocket knife, the soldier's knife. Swiss pocket knives are known all over the world.
34582.m: The Swiss pocket knife is world-famous.

34583.q: What does the army do during a big storm, for example?
34583.e: In disasters such as floods or avalanches the army helps. It then supports the fire brigade and civil defence.
34583.m: In disasters the army helps the population.

34584.q: Which part of the army protects Switzerland in the air?
34584.e: The air force protects Swiss airspace. It has fighter jets and helicopters.
34584.m: The air force protects the sky over Switzerland.

34585.q: Which squadron of the Swiss Air Force performs aerobatics in red aeroplanes?
34585.e: The Patrouille Suisse flies spectacular figures at air shows. The aeroplanes are painted red and white.
34585.m: The Patrouille Suisse performs aerobatics with red jets.

34586.q: What can a young man in Switzerland do instead of military service if it goes against his conscience?
34586.e: Anyone who cannot do military service because it goes against their conscience does civilian service. They then work in hospitals or care homes, for example.
34586.m: Instead of military service you can do civilian service.

34587.q: Who has to do military service in Switzerland?
34587.e: Military service is compulsory for Swiss men. Women can serve voluntarily.
34587.m: Swiss men have to do military service.

34588.q: What colour are the postboxes and vans of Swiss Post?
34588.e: Swiss Post's signature colour is yellow. Postboxes, vans and PostBuses are yellow.

34589.q: Which musical instrument is the symbol of the post?
34589.e: In the past the coachmen blew a horn when the mail coach arrived. The post horn is still the symbol of the post today.
34589.m: The post horn is the symbol of the post.

34590.q: What are the yellow Swiss Post buses that also go to mountain villages called?
34590.e: PostBuses drive over many passes and to remote villages. They are yellow.
34590.m: The yellow PostBus goes all the way to mountain villages.

34591.q: What does the PostBus horn sound like?
34591.e: The PostBus has a three-note horn. It sounds “Tü-ta-to” and can be heard clearly on mountain roads.

34592.q: How many digits does a Swiss postcode have?
34592.e: Swiss postcodes have four digits. Bern, for example, has the postcode 3000.
34592.m: A Swiss postcode has four digits.

34593.q: Which is faster for sending a letter in Switzerland?
34593.e: A letter sent by A-Post usually arrives the next working day. B-Post takes longer but is cheaper.
34593.m: A letter arrives faster by A-Post.

34594.q: Who brings letters and parcels to people's homes?
34594.e: Postwomen and postmen deliver the post. They often ride a small yellow electric vehicle.
34594.m: The postwoman brings the letters home.

34595.q: Which number do postcodes in the Zurich region begin with?
34595.e: The first digit shows the region. Postcodes in the Zurich area begin with 8, for example 8001.
34595.m: Postcodes in Zurich begin with an 8.

34596.q: In which country was the very first postage stamp in the world issued?
34596.e: The world's first postage stamp was the Penny Black from Great Britain in 1840. Other countries soon followed.
34596.m: The first postage stamp came from Great Britain in 1840.

34597.q: Which city issued Switzerland's first postage stamps in 1843?
34597.e: In 1843 the “Zurich 4 and 6” stamps appeared in Zurich. Geneva followed a little later.
34597.m: Switzerland's first postage stamps came from Zurich in 1843.

34598.q: Which children's charity in Switzerland sells special stamps with a surcharge?
34598.e: Pro Juventute helps children and young people. Part of the price of its stamps goes to this charity.
34598.m: Pro Juventute sells stamps that help children.

34599.q: What colour are the signposts on Swiss motorways?
34599.e: In Switzerland motorway signs are green. Main roads have blue signposts.
34599.m: Motorway signs in Switzerland are green.

34600.q: What is the maximum speed on Swiss motorways?
34600.e: The speed limit on Swiss motorways is 120 km/h. On roads outside built-up areas it is 80 km/h.
34600.m: The maximum speed on Swiss motorways is 120 km/h.

34601.q: What do you need in Switzerland to drive a car on the motorway?
34601.e: Anyone driving on Swiss motorways needs a motorway vignette. It comes as a sticker or electronically.
34601.m: You need a vignette for the motorway.

34602.q: How much does the motorway vignette cost per year in Switzerland (as of 2025)?
34602.e: The motorway vignette costs 40 francs. It is valid for a whole calendar year.

34603.q: Who is responsible for the national roads in Switzerland?
34603.e: The Confederation has been responsible for the national roads since 2008. Before that, mainly the cantons were responsible.
34603.m: The Confederation is responsible for the motorways.

34604.q: What is the motorway that runs from Geneva to Lake Constance called?
34604.e: The A1 runs from Geneva via Bern and Zurich to St Margrethen. It is the longest motorway in Switzerland.
34604.m: The A1 links Geneva with eastern Switzerland.

34605.q: What is the federal office that looks after the motorways called?
34605.e: ASTRA is the Federal Roads Office, FEDRO in English. It builds and maintains the national roads.

a: Money for goods brought across the border
Money for getting into the cinema
34606.e: Anyone who brings certain goods across the border has to pay money for them. This is called customs duty. Customs checks this at the border.
34606.m: You pay customs duty for goods brought across the border.

34607.q: How many countries does Switzerland border on?
34607.e: Switzerland borders on Germany, France, Italy, Austria and Liechtenstein.

34608.q: With which neighbouring country does Switzerland have no customs checks because they share a customs area?
34608.e: Liechtenstein and Switzerland have formed a shared customs area since 1924. That is why there are no customs on this border.
34608.m: There are no customs between Switzerland and Liechtenstein.

34609.q: What is the federal office that carries out checks at the Swiss border called?
a: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security
34609.e: Since 2022 the customs authority has been called the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security, FOCBS for short. It used to be called the Federal Customs Administration.

34610.q: Which animals help customs find hidden drugs?
34610.e: Customs dogs have a very fine sense of smell. They can sniff out drugs or money in suitcases.
34610.m: Customs dogs help customs with their fine noses.

34611.q: Up to what value per person can you bring back shopping from abroad without paying VAT (as of 2025)?
34611.e: Since 2025 the tax-free allowance has been 150 francs per person per day. Before that it was 300 francs.
34611.m: Private shopping from abroad up to 150 francs stays tax-free.

34612.q: Where are customs offices in Switzerland?
34612.e: Customs offices are on roads, at railway stations and at airports on the border. That is where you enter Switzerland.
34612.m: Customs offices are at the border.

34613.q: What is the abbreviation for the Swiss franc in trade?
34613.e: CHF stands for “Confoederatio Helvetica franc”. CH is the abbreviation for Switzerland.
34613.m: The Swiss franc is abbreviated to CHF.

34614.e: The 10-franc note is yellow. Its theme is time.

34615.e: The 100-franc note is blue. Its theme is water.

34616.q: Which banknote is the biggest in Switzerland?
34616.e: The biggest Swiss banknote is the 1,000-franc note. It is purple.
34616.m: The biggest Swiss banknote is the 1,000-franc note.

34618.q: Which coin is the biggest Swiss coin in everyday use?
34618.e: The 5-franc coin is the biggest and heaviest coin in everyday use. It is over 3 centimetres across.
34618.m: The 5-franc coin is the biggest Swiss coin.

34619.q: Which figure is on the 1-franc coin?
34619.e: Helvetia with a spear and shield is on the 1-franc and 2-franc coins. She is a symbol of Switzerland.
34619.m: Helvetia is on the franc coin.

34620.q: What is the big church in Bern with the tallest church tower in Switzerland called?
34620.e: The tower of Bern Minster is about 100 metres high. No other church tower in Switzerland is taller.
34620.m: Bern Minster has the tallest church tower in Switzerland.

34621.q: Which two languages are spoken in the canton of Bern?
34621.e: The canton of Bern is bilingual. In the Bernese Jura and in Biel people also speak French.
34621.m: People speak German and French in the canton of Bern.

34622.q: Which famous physicist lived in Bern around 1905?
34622.e: At that time Albert Einstein worked at the patent office in Bern. His flat on the Kramgasse is a museum today.
34622.m: Albert Einstein lived in Bern for a few years.

34623.q: Which short funicular runs down from near the Federal Palace to the district by the Aare?
34623.e: The Marzili funicular links the Federal Palace district with the Marzili by the Aare. It is one of the shortest funiculars in Switzerland.
34623.m: The Marzili funicular runs from the Federal Palace down to the Marzili.

34624.q: Which ducal family founded the city of Bern in 1191?
34624.e: Duke Berchtold V of Zähringen founded Bern in 1191. The Zähringens also founded other towns such as Fribourg.
34624.m: Bern was founded in 1191 by the Zähringens.

34625.q: What is the terrace on the south side of the Federal Palace with a view of the Aare called?
34625.e: The Bundesterrasse lies behind the Federal Palace, high above the Aare. In clear weather you can see as far as the Alps.
34625.m: The Bundesterrasse lies behind the Federal Palace.

34626.q: What stands out most about the outside of the Parliament Building in Bern?
34626.e: The Parliament Building has a big dome in the middle with a green copper roof. You can recognise the Federal Palace from far away because of it.
34626.m: The Parliament Building has a big green dome.

34627.q: Before it was rebuilt in 2004, what was the Bundesplatz mainly used for?
34627.e: For many years cars parked on the Bundesplatz. Since it was rebuilt in 2004 it has been an open square for people.
34627.m: The Bundesplatz used to be a car park.

34628.q: In summer water shoots out of the ground on the Bundesplatz in Bern. What does each of the 26 fountains stand for?
34628.e: There are 26 fountains, one for each canton. In summer lots of children play in the water there.
34628.m: The 26 fountains on the Bundesplatz stand for the 26 cantons.

34629.q: Which cantonal coat of arms was only added to the glass dome of the Federal Palace in 1981?
34629.e: When the Parliament Building was built, the canton of Jura did not exist yet. It was founded in 1979, and its coat of arms was added in 1981.
34629.m: The coat of arms of the canton of Jura was added to the dome later.

34630.q: What is the inner dome above the domed hall made of?
34630.e: The inner dome is made of coloured glass. That lets light into the domed hall.
34630.m: The inner dome of the Federal Palace is made of glass.

34631.q: What is the round, curved roof on top of the Federal Palace called?
34631.e: A dome is a round roof like half a ball. You can see the dome of the Federal Palace from far away.
34631.m: The round roof of the Federal Palace is called a dome.

34632.q: On which special day can you look round the Federal Palace freely without booking?
a: on the first day of school
34632.e: Parliament sometimes holds an open day. Then you can visit many rooms freely.
34632.m: On an open day the Federal Palace is open to everyone.

34633.q: Which bridge leads from Bern's old town straight to the bear pit?
34633.e: The Nydegg Bridge crosses the Aare. Right on the other side are the bear pit and the Bear Park.
34633.m: You reach the bear pit over the Nydegg Bridge.

34634.q: Who is mostly responsible for the police in Switzerland?
34634.e: The police are mainly a matter for the cantons. That is why every canton has a cantonal police force.
34634.m: The cantons are mostly responsible for the police.

34635.q: Which federal office warns the population about severe weather?
34635.e: MeteoSwiss is the Federal Office of Meteorology and Climatology. It makes weather forecasts and issues official severe weather warnings.

34636.q: What are the little teeth around the edge of a postage stamp called?
34636.e: The perforations come from small holes between the stamps. That makes them easy to tear off.
34636.m: The little teeth around the edge of a stamp are called perforations.

34637.q: Apart from the picture, what is shown on every postage stamp?
34637.e: Every stamp shows how much it is worth. That way you know how much postage has been paid.
34637.m: Every postage stamp shows its value.

34638.q: What is the best thing to pick up stamps with when collecting them?
34638.e: With tweezers the stamps do not get dirty or creased. Collectors use flat tweezers for this.
34638.m: Stamps are picked up with tweezers.

34639.q: Which coin can no longer be used to pay in Switzerland since 2007?
34639.e: The 1-centime coin was withdrawn at the end of 2006. It was too expensive to make.
34639.m: The 1-centime coin has not been valid since 2007.

34640.q: Which Latin words are written above the entrance of the Parliament Building?
34640.e: The words mean “Council house of the Swiss Confederation”. They are written in large letters on the gable above the entrance.
34640.m: “Curia Confoederationis Helveticae” is written above the entrance of the Federal Palace.

34641.q: How did people used to stick a stamp onto a letter?
a: They moistened the glue on the back
34641.e: Old stamps have a layer of glue on the back. When you moisten it, the stamp sticks.
34641.m: Old postage stamps have glue on the back.

34642.e: The 20-franc note is red. Its theme is light.

34643.q: Which canton does Federal Councillor Elisabeth Baume-Schneider come from?
34643.e: Elisabeth Baume-Schneider comes from the canton of Jura. She has been on the Federal Council since 2023.
34643.m: Elisabeth Baume-Schneider is a Federal Councillor from Jura.

34644.q: Which canton does Federal Councillor Beat Jans come from?
34644.e: Beat Jans was previously president of the government of Basel-Stadt. He was elected to the Federal Council in December 2023.
34644.m: Beat Jans is a Federal Councillor from Basel-Stadt.

34645.q: Since which year has the Federal Council existed?
34645.e: The Federal Council was created with the first Federal Constitution of 1848. Even then it had seven members.
34645.m: The Federal Council has existed since 1848.

34646.q: How many women are on the Federal Council in 2026?
34646.e: In 2026 Karin Keller-Sutter and Elisabeth Baume-Schneider are on the Federal Council. The other five members are men.
34646.m: In 2026 there are two women on the Federal Council.

34647.q: Which Federal Councillor from the canton of St Gallen is on the Federal Council in 2026?
34647.e: Karin Keller-Sutter comes from the canton of St Gallen. She has been on the Federal Council since 2019.
34647.m: Karin Keller-Sutter is a Federal Councillor from St Gallen.

34648.q: Which canton does Federal Councillor Ignazio Cassis come from?
34648.e: Ignazio Cassis comes from the canton of Ticino. His mother tongue is Italian.
34648.m: Ignazio Cassis is a Federal Councillor from Ticino.

34649.q: Which canton does Federal Councillor Albert Rösti come from?
34649.e: Albert Rösti comes from the Bernese Oberland in the canton of Bern. He has been on the Federal Council since 2023.
34649.m: Albert Rösti is a Federal Councillor from the canton of Bern.

34651.q: Who was newly elected to the Federal Council in 2025?
34651.e: Martin Pfister from the canton of Zug was elected in March 2025. That makes him the newest member of the Federal Council (as of 2026).
34651.m: Martin Pfister has been on the Federal Council since 2025.

34652.q: Who was President of the Confederation in 2024?
34652.e: Viola Amherd from Valais was President of the Confederation in 2024. At the time she headed the defence department.
34652.m: Viola Amherd was President of the Confederation in 2024.

34653.q: Who was President of the Confederation in 2025?
34653.e: Karin Keller-Sutter was President of the Confederation in 2025. It was her first year as president.
34653.m: Karin Keller-Sutter was President of the Confederation in 2025.

34654.q: Who was President of the Confederation in 2023?
34654.e: Alain Berset from the canton of Fribourg was President of the Confederation in 2023. It was his last year on the Federal Council.
34654.m: Alain Berset was President of the Confederation in 2023.

34655.q: Who was President of the Confederation in 2022?
34655.e: Ignazio Cassis was President of the Confederation for the first time in 2022.
34655.m: Ignazio Cassis was President of the Confederation in 2022.

34656.q: Is the President of the Confederation the boss of the other Federal Councillors?
a: No, he is first among equals
34656.e: The President of the Confederation has no more power than the others. People say he is “first among equals”.
34656.m: The President of the Confederation is first among equals, not the boss.

34657.q: Who stands in for the President of the Confederation when he cannot attend?
a: The President of the National Council
34657.e: There is the office of Vice-President for this. The Vice-President then takes over all the President's tasks.
34657.m: The Vice-President steps in when the President of the Confederation cannot attend.

34658.q: What does the Vice-President of the Federal Council usually become the following year?
34658.e: It is the custom that the Vice-President is elected President of the Confederation the following year. That way the chair passes round in turn.
34658.m: The Vice-President usually becomes President of the Confederation the following year.

34659.q: Which canton does President of the Confederation Guy Parmelin come from?
34659.e: Guy Parmelin is a winegrower and farmer from the canton of Vaud. His mother tongue is French.
34659.m: Guy Parmelin comes from the canton of Vaud.

34660.q: Who does the President of the Confederation welcome at the New Year reception in the Federal Palace?
a: All the school classes in Switzerland
34660.e: At the start of the year the President of the Confederation receives the diplomats of other countries. They wish each other a good year.
34660.m: At the New Year reception the President of the Confederation welcomes the ambassadors.

34661.q: Who was President of the Confederation in 2020?
34661.e: Simonetta Sommaruga was President of the Confederation in 2020, the year of the coronavirus pandemic. She had already held this office once in 2015.
34661.m: Simonetta Sommaruga was President of the Confederation in 2020.

34662.q: On which day does the presidential year begin?
34662.e: The presidential year is the same as the calendar year. It begins on 1 January and ends on 31 December.
34662.m: The presidential year begins on 1 January.

34663.q: In which month does Parliament elect the President of the Confederation for the next year?
34663.e: The election takes place during the winter session in December. That way everything is ready for the start at New Year.
34663.m: The President of the Confederation is elected in December.

34664.q: Can a President of the Confederation be president again straight away the next year?
a: Yes, as often as he likes
34664.e: The Federal Constitution forbids re-election for the following year. That way someone different gets a turn every year.
34664.m: Nobody may be President of the Confederation two years in a row.

34665.q: Who usually becomes President of the Confederation the following year?
a: The President of the Council of States
34665.e: The Vice-President usually takes over the presidency the next year. This is a long tradition.
34665.m: The Vice-President usually becomes President of the Confederation the next year.

34666.q: What happens to the President of the Confederation's department during the presidential year?
a: He has to give it up
34666.e: The President of the Confederation stays head of his department. The presidency is an extra task.
34666.m: During the presidential year the President of the Confederation keeps heading his department.

34667.q: How do the members of the Federal Council take their turn as president?
34667.e: According to an old tradition, the Federal Council takes turns with the presidency. Whoever has not been president for a long time will soon have their turn.
34667.m: The Federal Councillors take turns as President of the Confederation.

34668.q: How many times had Guy Parmelin been President of the Confederation by 2026?
34668.e: Guy Parmelin was President of the Confederation for the first time in 2021. In 2026 he is president for the second time.
34668.m: Guy Parmelin was President of the Confederation in 2021 and 2026.

34669.q: What is the person in charge of a department called?
34669.e: The person who leads a department is called the head of the department.
34669.m: The person in charge of a department is called the head of department.

a: A member of the Federal Council
A member of a cantonal government
The Chief of the Armed Forces
34670.e: Each of the seven Federal Council members is head of a department.
34670.m: Each department is headed by a member of the Federal Council.

34671.q: Which department is responsible for the army?
34671.e: The DDPS is the Federal Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport (VBS in German). The Swiss army belongs to it.
34671.m: The DDPS is responsible for the army.

34672.q: Which department looks after relations with other countries?
34672.e: The FDFA is the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs (EDA in German). It maintains contacts with other countries.
34672.m: The FDFA looks after relations with other countries.

34673.q: Which department does Karin Keller-Sutter head (as of 2026)?
34673.e: Karin Keller-Sutter heads the Federal Department of Finance (FDF). It looks after the Confederation's money.
34673.m: Karin Keller-Sutter is head of the finance department.

34674.q: Which department is responsible for transport, energy and the environment?
34674.e: DETEC stands for the Federal Department of the Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications (UVEK in German). This department looks after railways and roads, for example.
34674.m: DETEC is responsible for transport, energy and the environment.

34675.q: Which department is responsible for health and culture?
34675.e: The Federal Department of Home Affairs (FDHA) looks after health, culture and the AHV old-age insurance.
34675.m: The Department of Home Affairs looks after health and culture.

34676.q: Which department is responsible for justice and police?
34676.e: The FDJP is the Federal Department of Justice and Police (EJPD in German). Migration matters also belong to it.
34676.m: The FDJP is responsible for justice and police.

34677.q: Which department is responsible for the economy, education and farming?
34677.e: The EAER is the Federal Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research (WBF in German). Farming belongs to it too.
34677.m: The EAER looks after the economy, education and farming.

34678.q: How often is there a new official Federal Council photo?
34678.e: A new government photo is taken for each new year. So every photo looks a bit different.
34678.m: There is a new Federal Council photo every year.

34679.q: Apart from the seven Federal Council members, who else is in the official Federal Council photo?
a: The Chief of the Armed Forces
The President of the National Council
The President of the Federal Supreme Court
34679.e: The photo shows the seven Federal Council members and the Federal Chancellor. The Chancellor is a close part of the Federal Council's team.
34679.m: The Federal Chancellor is also in the Federal Council photo.

34680.q: Who decides what the Federal Council photo looks like?
34680.e: For this photo the President of the Confederation is a kind of director. He or she chooses the idea and the photographer.
34680.m: The President of the Confederation decides what the Federal Council photo looks like.

34681.q: When is the new Federal Council photo published?
a: At the start of the new year
34681.e: The new photo comes out at the start of the new year. That is also when a new presidential year begins.
34681.m: The new Federal Council photo comes out at the start of the year.

34682.q: How often is a new official Federal Council photo taken?
a: Only when the whole Council is re-elected
34682.e: There is a new official Federal Council photo every year. The President of the Confederation helps decide what it looks like.
34682.m: The Federal Council photo is taken anew every year.

34683.q: Where was the official 2026 Federal Council photo taken?
a: In the Federal Palace in Bern
34683.e: The photo was taken in the Federal Palace in the Salon de la Présidence, right next to the Federal Council's meeting room.
34683.m: The 2026 Federal Council photo was taken in the Federal Palace.

34684.q: Who publishes the official Federal Council photo?
34684.e: The Federal Chancellery publishes the new photo. It is the Federal Council's staff office.
34684.m: The Federal Chancellery publishes the Federal Council photo.

34685.q: Can you get a print of the official Federal Council photo?
34685.e: The Federal Council photo is there for everyone. You can order it as a print and also as individual portraits.
34685.m: Anyone can order the Federal Council photo.

34686.q: Who sits at the table with the seven members at Federal Council meetings?
a: The Chief of the Armed Forces
The President of the National Council
34686.e: The Federal Chancellor takes part in the meetings and may join in the discussion. But the Chancellor may not vote.
34686.m: The Federal Chancellor attends Federal Council meetings but does not vote.

34687.q: Has Switzerland ever had a woman as Federal Chancellor?
a: Yes, but only for one day
34687.e: Annemarie Huber-Hotz was the first female Federal Chancellor from 2000 to 2007. She was followed by Corina Casanova from 2008 to 2015.
34687.m: Switzerland has already had two female Federal Chancellors.

34688.e: The National Council and the Council of States elect the Federal Chancellor together. This joint assembly is called the Federal Assembly.
34688.m: The Federal Assembly elects the Federal Chancellor.

34689.q: May the Federal Chancellor vote in the Federal Council?
a: No, the Chancellor may only advise
Yes, the Chancellor's vote counts double
Yes, but only in a tie
34689.e: The Federal Chancellor attends the meetings and may give an opinion. But only the seven Federal Council members may vote.
34689.m: The Federal Chancellor advises the Federal Council but does not vote.

34690.q: Which office does the Federal Chancellor head?
34690.e: The Federal Chancellor is head of the Federal Chancellery. It helps the Federal Council with its work.
34690.m: The Federal Chancellor heads the Federal Chancellery.

34691.q: For how many years is the Federal Chancellor elected?
34691.e: The Federal Chancellor is elected for a term of four years. After that the Chancellor can be re-elected.
34691.m: The Federal Chancellor is elected for four years.

34693.q: Who helps the Federal Chancellor and informs the media as the Federal Council spokesperson?
a: A member of the National Council
The Chief of the Armed Forces
34693.e: The Federal Chancellor's deputies are called Vice-Chancellors. One of them is the spokesperson for the Federal Council.
34693.m: A Vice-Chancellor is the spokesperson for the Federal Council.

34694.q: On which day of the week does the Federal Council usually meet?
34694.e: The regular Federal Council meeting usually takes place on a Wednesday. It often lasts several hours.
34694.m: The Federal Council usually meets on Wednesdays.

34695.q: On which day of the week does the Federal Council meet during Parliament's sessions?
34695.e: During the sessions the Federal Councillors are often in Parliament. So they usually meet on a Friday then.
34695.m: During the sessions the Federal Council meets on Fridays.

34696.q: At what time does the Federal Council meeting usually begin?
34696.e: The meeting usually begins at 9 o'clock in the morning. It often lasts into the afternoon.
34696.m: The Federal Council meeting usually begins at 9 o'clock.

34697.q: Who chairs the Federal Council meeting?
a: The President of the National Council
34697.e: The President of the Confederation chairs the meeting. He or she sits at the front in the middle.
34697.m: The President of the Confederation chairs the Federal Council meeting.

34698.q: At least how many Federal Council members must be present for the Federal Council to make decisions?
34698.e: At least four of the seven members must be present. That is more than half.
34698.m: The Federal Council needs at least four members to make a decision.

34699.q: What happens in the Federal Council if there is a tie?
34699.e: If there is a tie, the vote of the President of the Confederation counts double. That is what the law says.
34699.m: In a tie, the President of the Confederation's vote decides.

34700.q: What is the room called where the Federal Council holds its meetings?
34700.e: The Federal Council meets in the Federal Council Room in the Federal Palace West. The room has a chandelier from 1857.
34700.m: The Federal Council meets in the Federal Council Room.

34701.q: Which language do the Federal Councillors speak at their meeting?
34701.e: Each member speaks in their own national language, for example German, French or Italian. The Federal Council's website says so too.
34701.m: In the Federal Council each member speaks their own language.

34702.q: What is the Federal Council's annual outing jokingly called?
34702.e: Because the Federal Councillors go on an outing together, people also call it the “Federal Council's school trip”.
34702.m: The Federal Council's outing is jokingly called its school trip.

34703.q: How long does the Federal Council's outing last?
34703.e: The Federal Council's outing is a two-day trip. The Federal Council gets to know a region of Switzerland.
34703.m: The Federal Council's outing lasts two days.

34704.q: Who invites the others on the Federal Council's outing?
34704.e: The person holding the presidency invites the other Federal Council members. He or she also plans the programme.
34704.m: The President of the Confederation invites the others on the Federal Council's outing.

34705.q: Where does the Federal Council's outing usually go?
34705.e: Since 1961 the outing has usually gone to the home canton of the President of the Confederation.
34705.m: The Federal Council's outing usually goes to the President's home canton.

34706.q: When in the year does the Federal Council's outing take place?
34706.e: The outing begins after the last meeting before the summer holidays. That is usually in early July.
34706.m: The Federal Council's outing takes place before the summer holidays.

34707.q: Who goes on the annual Federal Council outing?
a: All the Federal Council members and the Federal Chancellor
Only the President of the Confederation
All members of the National Council
34707.e: Once a year the whole Federal Council goes on an outing together with the Federal Chancellor. On the way they also meet members of the public.
34707.m: The whole Federal Council goes on the outing.

34708.q: What does the Federal Council often do together with the public on the outing?
a: It has drinks and snacks with them
34708.e: On the outing the Federal Council often invites people for drinks and snacks, an apéro. There people can meet the Federal Councillors and talk to them.
34708.m: On the outing the Federal Council meets people over drinks and snacks.

34710.q: Who gives the speech to the population on New Year's Day?
a: The Chief of the Armed Forces
34710.e: Traditionally the President of the Confederation addresses the population on New Year's Day.
34710.m: The President of the Confederation gives the New Year speech.

34711.q: On which day is the New Year speech broadcast?
34711.e: The New Year speech is broadcast on the first day of the new year.
34711.m: The New Year speech is on 1 January.

34712.q: Where can you see and hear the New Year speech?
34712.e: The speech is broadcast on radio and television. You can also find it on the internet.
34712.m: The New Year speech is on television and radio.

34713.q: How often does the office of President of the Confederation change hands?
34713.e: Every year the Federal Assembly elects a different member of the Federal Council as President of the Confederation. This person also gives the New Year speech.

34714.q: When is the New Year speech recorded?
34714.e: The speech is recorded a few days beforehand. That way it can be broadcast on New Year's Day.
34714.m: The New Year speech is recorded before New Year.

34715.q: How do you wish someone a happy New Year in French?
34715.e: “Bonne année” means “Happy New Year”. That is how people in French-speaking Switzerland wish each other a happy New Year.

34716.q: How do you wish someone a happy New Year in Italian?
34716.e: “Buon anno” means “Good year”. That is how people in Italian-speaking Switzerland wish each other a happy New Year.

34717.q: Who chooses the place where the New Year speech is recorded?
34717.e: The person holding the presidency chooses the place themselves. It is often a place that has a special meaning for them.
34717.m: The President of the Confederation chooses the place for the New Year speech.

34718.q: Who leads the Federal Council election in Parliament?
a: The head of the National Council
34718.e: The election is led by the President of the National Council, who then chairs the United Federal Assembly.
34718.m: The head of the National Council leads the Federal Council election.

34719.q: Who can be elected to the Federal Council?
a: Any Swiss citizen who can vote
Only members of the National Council
34719.e: Anyone who can be elected to the National Council can be elected. That means all Swiss citizens who are entitled to vote.
34719.m: All Swiss citizens entitled to vote can be elected to the Federal Council.

34720.q: When is the whole Federal Council elected again?
34720.e: The whole Federal Council is re-elected in the winter session after the National Council elections. This is called the general renewal.
34720.m: After the National Council elections the whole Federal Council is elected again.

34721.q: What is a person asked straight after being elected to the Federal Council?
34721.e: The President of the Council asks whether the person accepts the election. Only with a yes is the election valid.
34721.m: A person who has been elected must say whether they accept.

34722.q: How do the members of Parliament vote in the Federal Council election?
34722.e: The election is secret. Each member writes a name on a ballot paper.
34722.m: The Federal Council election is secret.

34723.q: How many votes do you need to be elected to the Federal Council?
34723.e: You need an absolute majority. That means more than half of the valid votes.
34723.m: To be elected you need more than half of the votes.

34724.q: In the general renewal of the Federal Council, who is elected first?
a: Whoever has been in office longest
Whoever comes first in the alphabet
34724.e: The existing members are elected in order of how long they have been in office. Whoever has been there longest comes first.
34724.m: In the Federal Council election, whoever has been in office longest comes first.

34725.q: When was the last general election of the whole Federal Council (as of 2026)?
34725.e: On 13 December 2023 the whole Federal Council was re-elected. The next general renewal is in December 2027.
34725.m: The last general renewal of the Federal Council was in December 2023.

34726.q: What must newly elected Federal Councillors take in front of Parliament?
34726.e: Newly elected members solemnly promise before the Federal Assembly to carry out their office well. This is called the oath of office or the solemn promise.
34726.m: Newly elected Federal Councillors take the oath of office.

34727.e: “Extra muros” is Latin. It means a meeting held outside the Federal Palace.

34728.q: Where does the Federal Council meet for an extra muros meeting?
34728.e: For an extra muros meeting, the Federal Council travels to a canton and holds its meeting there.
34728.m: For an extra muros meeting, the Federal Council visits a canton.

34729.q: What do the Latin words “extra muros” mean?
34729.e: “Extra muros” means outside the walls. The Federal Council then does not meet in the Federal Palace but somewhere else in Switzerland.

34730.q: Why does the Federal Council hold extra muros meetings?
a: To be close to the people in the regions
Because the Federal Palace is closed
Because the law demands it every week
34730.e: With these meetings the Federal Council shows that it is there for the whole of Switzerland. It visits different regions and meets the people.
34730.m: With extra muros meetings the Federal Council visits the regions.

34731.q: Where does the Federal Council meet for an extra muros meeting?
a: In the Federal Council room in Bern
34731.e: For an extra muros meeting, the Federal Council travels to a canton and meets there. This brings it closer to the people.
34731.m: Extra muros, the Federal Council meets outside Bern.

34732.q: What can people do after an extra muros meeting?
a: They can meet the Federal Councillors
They must vote on a law
They get a day off school
They may vote in the Federal Council
34732.e: After the meeting there is usually a drinks reception. People can ask the Federal Councillors questions.
34732.m: At extra muros meetings the Federal Council gets close to the people.

34733.q: Roughly how often does the Federal Council hold an extra muros meeting?
34733.e: Normally the Federal Council meets every week in Bern. About once a year it travels to another canton for a meeting.
34733.m: About once a year the Federal Council meets extra muros.

34734.q: What stays the same at an extra muros meeting as at a meeting in Bern?
34734.e: Even outside Bern, the Federal Council discusses behind closed doors. Only afterwards does it meet the people.
34734.m: Even extra muros, the Federal Council discusses in confidence.

34735.q: What is the longest time someone may be a member of the Federal Council?
34735.e: There is no term limit. A member can be re-elected again and again until they step down.
34735.m: There is no fixed maximum time in office for Federal Councillors.

34736.q: Which Federal Councillor stepped down at the end of 2022?
34736.e: Simonetta Sommaruga left the Federal Council at the end of 2022. She had been in office since 2010.
34736.m: Simonetta Sommaruga stepped down at the end of 2022.

34737.q: What is the election of a new person called when a Federal Council member steps down?
34737.e: In a by-election, Parliament elects someone for the seat that has become free.
34737.m: After someone steps down, there is a by-election.

34738.q: Who elects the successor when a member of the Federal Council steps down?
a: The people at the ballot box
The rest of the Federal Council
34738.e: After a resignation, the United Federal Assembly, that is the National Council and the Council of States together, elects a successor.
34738.m: Parliament elects the successor in the Federal Council.

34739.q: Which Federal Councillor announced in October 2026 that he would step down at the end of 2026?
34739.e: Guy Parmelin announced on 2 October 2026 that he would step down at the end of 2026. Parliament then elects a successor.
34739.m: Guy Parmelin is leaving the Federal Council at the end of 2026.

34740.q: Which Federal Councillor stepped down in spring 2025?
34740.e: Viola Amherd from Valais stepped down at the end of March 2025. She had been in the Federal Council since 2019.
34740.m: Viola Amherd stepped down in spring 2025.

34741.q: Who decides which department a new Federal Council member takes over?
34741.e: After an election, the Federal Council shares out the departments itself. Sometimes existing members also change department.
34741.m: The Federal Council shares out the departments itself.

34742.q: How many years will Guy Parmelin have been in the Federal Council when he steps down at the end of 2026?
34742.e: Guy Parmelin took office at the start of 2016. Up to the end of 2026 that makes eleven years.
34742.m: Guy Parmelin was a Federal Councillor for eleven years.

34743.q: Whom does the National Council mainly represent?
34743.e: The National Council represents the people. That is why it is also called the people's chamber.
34743.m: The National Council represents the Swiss people.

34744.q: Who elects the members of the National Council?
34744.e: The people in Switzerland who have the right to vote elect the National Council. The election takes place in each canton.
34744.m: The voters elect the National Council.

34745.q: When was the last National Council election (as of 2026)?
34745.e: The federal elections took place on 22 October 2023. The next ones are in autumn 2027.
34745.m: The National Council was last elected in October 2023.

34746.q: Where does a National Council member stand when speaking in the council?
34746.e: Anyone who wants to speak in the National Council goes to the front, to the lectern. That way everyone can see and hear the person well.
34746.m: In the National Council you speak from the lectern.

34747.q: In which three languages can you hear National Council debates interpreted?
34747.e: In the National Council there is simultaneous interpreting into German, French and Italian. The interpreters work in booths.
34747.m: In the National Council, interpreting is into German, French and Italian.

34748.q: What are both chambers called together?
34748.e: The National Council and the Council of States together form the Federal Assembly. It is the Swiss Parliament.
34748.m: The National Council and the Council of States together form the Federal Assembly.

34749.q: What does Parliament in Bern mainly decide on?
34749.e: Parliament makes and changes the federal laws. It also decides on the money the Confederation spends.
34749.m: Parliament in Bern makes Switzerland's laws.

34750.q: Where does the German name “Ständerat” (Council of States) come from?
a: from “Stand”, an old word for canton
from “Stadt” (town), because it meets in towns
34750.e: In the past the cantons were also called “Stände”. That is where the Council of States gets its German name.
34750.m: “Stand” is an old German word for canton.

34751.q: Are the National Council and the Council of States equally important?
a: No, the Council of States decides alone.
No, the National Council decides alone.
34751.e: In Switzerland both chambers have equal rights. A law only applies if both councils agree.
34751.m: A law needs the approval of the National Council and the Council of States.

34752.q: Where do members of the Council of States speak from in a debate?
34752.e: In the Council of States, members stand up at their seat and speak from there. The chamber is smaller than the National Council chamber.
34752.m: In the Council of States you speak from your own seat.

34753.q: What does the large mural in the Council of States chamber show?
34753.e: The large mural in the Council of States chamber shows a Landsgemeinde. Many people gather there in the open air and vote.
34753.m: In the Council of States chamber, a mural shows a Landsgemeinde.

34754.q: In which canton is the member of the Council of States elected at the Landsgemeinde?
34754.e: In Appenzell Innerrhoden the voters elect their member of the Council of States at the Landsgemeinde. There people vote in the open air by raising their hands.
34754.m: Appenzell Innerrhoden elects its member of the Council of States at the Landsgemeinde.

34755.q: Who decides how the Council of States election works in a canton?
34755.e: The Federal Constitution leaves the rules for the Council of States election to the cantons. That is why the election is not the same everywhere.
34755.m: Each canton organises the election to the Council of States itself.

34756.q: Why does Zurich have many more seats in the National Council than Uri?
34756.e: The seats in the National Council are shared out according to the number of inhabitants. Large cantons therefore get more seats.
34756.m: Cantons with many inhabitants have more seats in the National Council.

34757.q: Which canton has the most seats in the National Council (as of 2023)?
34757.e: Zurich is the canton with the most inhabitants. In the 2023 election it had 36 seats.
34757.m: Zurich has the most seats in the National Council.

34758.q: Why does the canton of Zurich have more National Council seats than the canton of Uri?
a: Because many more people live in Zurich
Because Zurich has a larger area
34758.e: The seats in the National Council are shared out according to population. In 2023 Zurich had 36 seats, Uri only one.
34758.m: More inhabitants mean more National Council seats.

34759.q: What is the smallest number of National Council seats each canton has?
34759.e: The Constitution guarantees every canton at least one seat in the National Council. So even the smallest canton is represented.
34759.m: Every canton has at least one seat in the National Council.

34760.q: How many seats do the National Council and the Council of States have together?
34760.e: The National Council has 200 members and the Council of States 46. 200 plus 46 makes 246.
34760.m: The Federal Assembly has 246 members in total.

34761.q: How many National Council members are more than half?
34761.e: Half of 200 is 100. So a majority of all members needs at least 101.
34761.m: With 200 members, 101 votes or more is more than half.

34762.q: Which canton had the most seats in the National Council after Zurich in the 2023 election?
34762.e: In the 2023 election Bern had 24 seats in total. That is the second most after Zurich.
34762.m: Bern is the canton with the second most seats in the National Council.

34763.q: How many seats does the canton of Bern have in the Council of States?
34763.e: Most cantons send two members to the Council of States. This is the same for large and small cantons, so also for Bern.
34763.m: Most cantons have two seats in the Council of States.

34764.q: How many cantons have only one seat in the Council of States?
34764.e: Six cantons have only one seat. They are the former half-cantons.
34764.m: Six cantons have only one seat in the Council of States.

34765.q: Which canton has only one seat in the Council of States?
34765.e: Basel-Stadt is a former half-canton. That is why it has only one seat in the Council of States.
34765.m: Basel-Stadt has one seat in the Council of States.

34766.q: How many seats do Obwalden and Nidwalden have together in the Council of States?
34766.e: Obwalden and Nidwalden each have one seat in the Council of States. Together that makes 2 seats.
34766.m: Obwalden and Nidwalden each have one seat in the Council of States.

34767.q: Does Uri have as many seats in the Council of States as Zurich?
34767.e: In the Council of States the number of inhabitants does not count. Uri and Zurich each have 2 seats there.
34767.m: In the Council of States, small and large cantons have the same number of seats.

34768.q: Which canton has two seats in the Council of States?
34768.e: Glarus is a full canton and therefore has two seats. The other three cantons are former half-cantons with only one seat.
34768.m: Glarus has two seats in the Council of States.

34769.q: What is the period called when Parliament meets in Bern?
34769.e: Parliament meets several times a year for a few weeks. This period is called a session.
34769.m: A session is the time when Parliament meets.

34770.q: Roughly how long does an ordinary session last?
34770.e: An ordinary session lasts about three weeks. After that the members return to their jobs.
34770.m: A session lasts about three weeks.

34771.e: The four sessions are called the spring, summer, autumn and winter sessions. They are named after the seasons.
34771.m: The sessions are named after the seasons.

34772.q: What happens on the last Friday of a session?
34772.e: On the last day the councils take their final vote on the finished laws. These are called the final votes.
34772.m: At the end of every session there are final votes.

34773.q: What is an extra session outside the usual four called?
34773.e: When there is a lot of business, a special session can take place. It is in addition to the four ordinary sessions.
34773.m: A special session is an additional session.

34774.q: In which city does the Swiss Parliament meet?
34774.e: The Swiss Parliament meets in the Federal Palace in Bern. There the politicians discuss new laws.
34774.m: Parliament meets in the Federal Palace in Bern.

34775.q: Who meets in the National Council chamber?
34775.e: The National Council has its own chamber in the Federal Palace. It is called the National Council chamber.
34775.m: The National Council meets in the National Council chamber.

34776.q: Where does the United Federal Assembly meet?
a: in the Council of States chamber
34776.e: When both councils meet together, they need the largest chamber. That is why they meet in the National Council chamber.
34776.m: The United Federal Assembly meets in the National Council chamber.

34777.q: What does the large mural in the National Council chamber show?
34777.e: The large picture behind the presiding officers shows the landscape at Lake Uri. You can see the Rütli, the village of Schwyz and the Mythen peaks.
34777.m: The mural in the National Council chamber shows the area around the Rütli.

34779.q: Who elects the Federal Council in the National Council chamber?
34779.e: The members of the National Council and the Council of States elect the Federal Council together. For this they meet in the National Council chamber.
34779.m: The United Federal Assembly elects the Federal Council.

34780.q: Who sits under the cantonal coats of arms on the back wall of the National Council chamber?
a: the members of the Council of States
34780.e: At the United Federal Assembly, the members of the Council of States sit at the back of the chamber. Above every two seats there is a wooden arch with the coat of arms of their canton.
34780.m: The members of the Council of States sit under their cantonal coats of arms in the National Council chamber.

34781.q: Who meets every year for the Youth Session in the National Council chamber?
a: Young people from all over Switzerland
34781.e: The first Federal Youth Session took place in 1991. Today young people debate in the Federal Palace every year and play at being Parliament.
34781.m: At the Youth Session, young people may debate in the National Council chamber.

34782.q: How do the members sit in the National Council chamber?
34782.e: National Council members sit arranged by parliamentary group. People in the same group sit close together.
34782.m: In the National Council chamber, the parliamentary groups sit together.

34783.q: What is on the desk of the President of the National Council?
34783.e: On the President's desk there is a small hand bell. The chair uses it to get people's attention.
34783.m: The council President has a small bell on the desk.

34784.q: Why does the council President ring the bell?
a: so that the chamber becomes quiet
so that the lights come on
34784.e: When it is noisy in the chamber, the President rings the bell. That is how he asks for quiet and attention.
34784.m: With the bell, the council President asks for quiet.

34785.q: How does the President of the National Council traditionally open a session?
34785.e: At the beginning, the President rings the small bell. This is how the session is rung in.
34785.m: A session in the National Council is rung in with the bell.

34786.q: For how long is someone President of the National Council?
34786.e: The President is elected anew every year. This way different people get a turn.
34786.m: The council President changes every year.

34787.q: What is the person at the head of the National Council often called?
34787.e: The President of the National Council is often called the “highest Swiss citizen”. In terms of protocol, the office ranks at the very top.
34787.m: The President of the National Council is regarded as the highest Swiss citizen.

34788.q: What does the council President do when a vote is tied?
34788.e: Normally the President does not vote. But in a tie her vote decides; this is the casting vote.
34788.m: In a tie, the council President has the casting vote.

34789.q: What does the council President mainly do during a sitting?
34789.e: The President gives people the floor, keeps an eye on the time and leads the votes. The bell helps him do this.
34789.m: The council President chairs the sittings of the council.

34790.q: Why does the President of the National Council ring the small bell during the sitting?
a: To bring quiet to the chamber
34790.e: When it gets too noisy in the chamber, the President rings the bell. That is how she asks for quiet and attention.
34790.m: With the bell, the council President brings quiet.

34791.q: Which three buttons does each council member have for voting?
34791.e: At every seat there are buttons for Yes, No and Abstain. The system counts the votes immediately.
34791.m: In the council you vote Yes, No or Abstain.

34792.q: What does it mean if you press the “Abstain” button?
a: you vote neither Yes nor No
34792.e: When you abstain, you say neither Yes nor No. You take part in the vote without committing yourself.
34792.m: An abstention is neither Yes nor No.

34793.q: How do National Council members vote in the chamber today?
34793.e: In the National Council chamber, every member has buttons for Yes, No and Abstain. The result appears immediately on a large display board.
34793.m: The National Council votes using buttons.

34794.q: The National Council has voted electronically since 1994, the Council of States only since 2014. How many years later did the Council of States join in?
34794.e: 2014 minus 1994 makes 20 years. The Council of States carried on voting by raising hands for a long time.
34794.m: The Council of States has only voted electronically since 2014.

34795.q: Where can you see the result of a vote in the chamber?
a: on a note in the letterbox
34795.e: After the vote, the result appears on screens in the chamber. How each member voted is shown too.
34795.m: The result of a vote appears on screens in the chamber.

34796.q: Can you look up how a National Council member voted?
a: Only the Federal Council may know.
34796.e: Since 2007 all votes in the National Council have been published with names. So you can see who voted Yes, No or Abstain.
34796.m: How council members vote is public.

34797.q: Who may press the voting button at a seat?
a: only the member whose seat it is
the person sitting next to them
34797.e: Every council member must vote at their own seat. Pressing the button for someone else is not allowed.
34797.m: Every council member votes only for themselves.

34798.q: What does the electronic system count in a vote?
34798.e: The system counts all the Yes votes, No votes and abstentions. It also saves the results.
34798.m: The voting system counts the votes immediately.

34799.q: What is a woman who sits in the National Council called?
34799.e: Both men and women in the National Council are called National Councillors. They are all members of Parliament.
34799.m: A woman in the National Council is a National Councillor.

34800.q: What is a woman who sits in the Council of States called?
a: Member of the Council of States
34800.e: Women in the Council of States are members of the Council of States. They represent their canton in Bern.
34800.m: A woman in the Council of States is a member of the Council of States.

34801.q: Since which year can women be elected to the National Council?
34801.e: In 1971 Swiss women got the right to vote and stand for election at federal level. Since then they can be elected to Parliament.
34801.m: Since 1971 women can be elected to the Federal Parliament.

34802.q: Since which year can women be elected to the National Council and the Council of States?
34802.e: In 1971 women in Switzerland got the right to vote and stand for election at federal level. Since then they can also be elected to Parliament.
34802.m: Since 1971 women can be elected to the Federal Parliament.

34803.q: What does the President of the National Council do?
a: They chair the sittings of the National Council
They lead the Federal Supreme Court
34803.e: The President of the National Council chairs the debates in the council and is elected anew every year. In 1977 Elisabeth Blunschy was the first woman to hold this office.
34803.m: The President of the National Council chairs the sittings of the National Council.

34804.q: What do most members of Parliament do besides Parliament?
a: They live in the Federal Palace.
34804.e: For many members, politics is not a full-time job. Alongside it they work, for example, as a farmer, a lawyer or a teacher.
34804.m: Many members of Parliament have a job besides Parliament.

34805.q: What do you call a parliament in which the members usually also have a job?
34805.e: In Switzerland politics is a side job for many members. That is why people speak of a militia parliament.

34806.q: What is the Wandelhalle in the Federal Palace?
a: a large hall next to the National Council chamber
34806.e: The Wandelhalle (lobby hall) is on the south side of the National Council chamber. Council members and guests meet there.
34806.m: The Wandelhalle is next to the National Council chamber.

34807.q: What do council members often use the Wandelhalle for?
34807.e: In the Wandelhalle council members talk to guests, journalists and representatives of associations. Receptions are held there too.
34807.m: Council members have many conversations in the Wandelhalle.

34808.q: What are people called who try to win council members over to their cause in the Wandelhalle?
34808.e: Lobbyists represent the interests of companies or associations. They often meet council members in the Wandelhalle.
34808.m: Lobbyists try to persuade council members.

34809.q: Where does the word “lobby” get its name from?
34809.e: “Lobby” is an English word for an entrance hall. People waited in such halls for the members of parliament.
34809.m: The word “lobby” originally means an entrance hall.

34810.q: In which building in Bern is the Wandelhalle?
34810.e: The Wandelhalle is in the Federal Palace, right next to the National Council chamber. Council members and guests meet there.
34810.m: The Wandelhalle is in the Federal Palace in Bern.

34811.q: When is the Wandelhalle especially busy?
34811.e: During the session, the National Council and Council of States meet in the Federal Palace. Then many council members, guests and journalists meet in the Wandelhalle.
34811.m: During the session the Wandelhalle is very busy.

34812.q: Who often meets council members in the Wandelhalle for interviews?
34812.e: During the session many media people are in the Federal Palace. In the Wandelhalle they ask the council members questions.
34812.m: Council members often give interviews in the Wandelhalle.

34813.q: From where can visitors follow the debates in the National Council chamber?
34813.e: Above the chamber there are galleries for the public. From there you can see and hear the council.
34813.m: Visitors follow the debates from the public gallery.

34814.q: How much does a visit to the public gallery during the session cost?
34814.e: Following the debates is free of charge. Visiting the dome hall costs nothing either.
34814.m: A visit to the public gallery in the Federal Palace is free.

34815.q: What must visitors hand in at the security check?
34815.e: At the security check you leave an official ID such as an identity card or passport. You get it back when you leave.
34815.m: You need an ID to visit the public gallery.

34816.q: Are you allowed to take photos from the public gallery?
34816.e: Photos and films are not allowed from the galleries. This way the debates are not disturbed.
34816.m: You must not take photos in the public gallery.

34817.q: What do visitors get if they want to hear the interpretation of the debate?
34817.e: National Council debates are interpreted simultaneously. Visitors get headphones for this free of charge.
34817.m: With headphones you can hear the interpretation of the debate.

34818.q: From where do visitors to the Federal Palace watch the debates in the National Council?
34818.e: Visitors sit up in the public gallery. From there they look down into the chamber where the members of Parliament are debating.
34818.m: Visitors follow the debates from the public gallery.

34819.q: In which city is the Federal Square (Bundesplatz)?
34819.e: The Federal Square is right in front of the Federal Palace in Bern. Markets and festivals often take place there.
34819.m: The Federal Square is in front of the Federal Palace in Bern.

34820.q: What can you see in the coloured glass of the large dome of the Federal Palace?
a: The coats of arms of the cantons
The faces of the Federal Councillors
34820.e: In the middle, the glass dome shows the Swiss cross. All around it you can see the coats of arms of the cantons.
34820.m: The coats of arms of the cantons shine in the dome of the Federal Palace.

a: a group with similar political ideas
34821.e: In a party, people with similar views join together. They want to have a say in politics together.
34821.m: A political party is a group with similar political ideas.

34822.q: What does a party do before the elections?
34822.e: Parties look for people who would like to be elected. These people then appear on their lists. The votes are counted by the election office.
34822.m: Parties put forward candidates for the elections.

34823.q: Which party has had the most seats in the National Council since the 2023 election?
34823.e: The SVP won 62 seats in 2023. That is more than any other party.
34823.m: Since 2023 the SVP has been the largest party in the National Council.

34824.q: Which party came second in the 2023 National Council election?
34824.e: The SP won 41 seats in 2023. Only the SVP had more.
34824.m: In 2023 the SP became the second largest party in the National Council.

34825.q: What do you call a group of council members who work together?
34825.e: A parliamentary group is a group of members of Parliament with similar opinions. It can be made up of one or several parties.
34825.m: Council members with similar ideas form a parliamentary group.

34826.q: What is the minimum number of members from one council that a parliamentary group needs?
34826.e: A parliamentary group needs at least five members from the same council. Groups may, for example, take part in the committees.
34826.m: A parliamentary group needs at least five members from one council.

34827.q: How many parties are there in the Federal Council (as of 2026)?
34827.e: The Federal Council has members from the SVP, SP, FDP and the Centre. That makes four parties.
34827.m: Four parties are represented in the Federal Council.

34828.q: Which party had the third most seats in the National Council in 2023, after the SVP and SP?
34828.e: The Centre won 29 seats in 2023. The FDP had 28 and the Greens 23 seats.
34828.m: In 2023 the Centre was the third largest party in the National Council.

34829.q: In which month does the winter session end?
34829.e: The winter session begins at the end of November and lasts into December. In this session Parliament also elects new presidents.
34829.m: The winter session takes place at the end of November and in December.

34830.q: How is the Council of States elected in most cantons?
a: by the people of the canton
34830.e: In the cantons, the people elect their members of the Council of States directly. In the past, the cantonal parliaments still elected them in some cantons.
34830.m: The people of a canton elect its members of the Council of States.

34831.q: What can you watch from the public gallery in the Federal Palace?
a: The meetings of the Federal Council
Hearings of the Federal Supreme Court
34831.e: From the public gallery you can follow debates and votes in the council. The meetings of the Federal Council, on the other hand, are not public.
34831.m: In the public gallery you can watch debates and votes live.

34833.q: Is the Wandelhalle a place for voting?
a: No, people talk there, they do not vote.
Yes, the National Council votes there.
Yes, the Council of States meets there.
34833.e: Votes only take place in the council chambers. The Wandelhalle is a place for conversations and meetings.
34833.m: In the Wandelhalle people talk; voting happens in the chamber.

34834.q: What are the small groups called in which council members prepare the business?
34834.e: Before an item of business comes to the council, a committee discusses it. There a few council members work on it in more detail.
34834.m: Committees prepare the business for the council.

34835.q: Since which year has the Council of States met in today's Parliament Building?
34835.e: The Parliament Building in Bern was finished in 1902. Since then the National Council and the Council of States have met there.
34835.m: The Parliament Building in Bern has been in use since 1902.

34836.q: How many seats does the canton of Uri have in the National Council?
34836.e: Uri has only a few inhabitants. That is why the canton has only one seat in the National Council.
34836.m: Uri has one seat in the National Council.

34837.q: Which canton is the youngest canton in the Council of States?
34837.e: The canton of Jura has only existed since 1979. Since then, like most cantons, it has had two seats in the Council of States.
34837.m: Jura is the youngest canton in Switzerland.

34838.q: Parliament meets 4 times a year, for 3 weeks each time. How many weeks is that altogether?
34838.e: 4 times 3 weeks is 12 weeks. That is how long Parliament meets in Bern every year.

34839.q: How did the Council of States usually vote before the electronic system?
34839.e: In the past, members of the Council of States showed their vote by raising their hand. Vote counters then counted the hands.
34839.m: In the past the Council of States voted by raising hands.

34840.q: Who may enter the Wandelhalle during the session?
a: Council members and guests with a pass
34840.e: During the session the Wandelhalle is not open to everyone. Council members and people with an access pass, for example invited guests or media people, may enter.
34840.m: During the session you can only enter the Wandelhalle with a pass.

34841.q: Why do many people hang up the Swiss flag on 1 August?
34841.e: 1 August is the national holiday. With the flag, people show that they are joining in the celebration.
34841.m: On 1 August many people decorate their house with the flag.

34842.q: What shape is the Swiss flag on land?
34842.e: The Swiss flag is square, so it is as tall as it is wide. This is very rare for national flags.
34842.m: The Swiss flag is a square.

34843.q: Which other country apart from Switzerland also has a square flag?
34843.e: Only Switzerland and Vatican City have a square national flag.
34843.m: The Vatican also has a square flag.

34844.q: Does the Swiss cross touch the edge of the flag?
a: No, it stands free in the middle
Yes, only at the top and bottom
Yes, only on the left and right
34844.e: The Swiss cross stands free in the middle of the flag. It does not touch the edge.
34844.m: The Swiss cross floats free in the middle.

34845.q: Which symbol on goods often shows that they come from Switzerland?
34845.e: Many Swiss products carry the Swiss cross. It shows that they come from Switzerland.
34845.m: The Swiss cross stands for goods from Switzerland.

34846.q: Which aid organisation has a red cross on a white background as its symbol?
34846.e: The Red Cross was founded in Switzerland. To honour Switzerland, its flag was used with the colours swapped round.
34846.m: The Red Cross symbol is the Swiss flag reversed.

34847.q: Who founded the Red Cross, whose symbol is reminiscent of the Swiss flag?
34847.e: Henry Dunant inspired the founding of the Red Cross. For this he received the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901.
34847.m: Henry Dunant from Geneva founded the Red Cross.

34848.q: What shape is the Swiss flag on ships?
34848.e: On ships a rectangular Swiss flag flies. That is the usual practice everywhere on the water.
34848.m: On ships the Swiss flag is rectangular.

34849.q: What are the two national colours of Switzerland?
34849.e: Switzerland's national colours are red and white, as in its flag.
34849.m: The Swiss national colours are red and white.

34850.q: Which canton has a red coat of arms with a small white cross in the corner?
34850.e: The coat of arms of Schwyz is red with a small white cross at the top left. The name Schweiz (Switzerland) comes from the name Schwyz too.
34850.m: The Schwyz coat of arms is red with a small white cross.

34851.q: What colour do Swiss fans usually wear at an international match?
34851.e: The fans show the national colour red. The national football team usually plays in red shirts too.
34851.m: Swiss fans like to wear red.

34852.q: Apart from white, what colour is the coat of arms of the canton of Solothurn?
34852.e: The coat of arms of Solothurn is red at the top and white at the bottom. So it has the same colours as the Swiss flag.
34852.m: Solothurn has a red and white coat of arms.

34853.q: What two colours does the coat of arms of the canton of Ticino have?
34853.e: The Ticino coat of arms is red on the left and blue on the right. So it does not have the national colours.
34853.m: The Ticino coat of arms is red and blue.

34855.q: What colour is the diagonal stripe in the Bern coat of arms?
34855.e: The Bern coat of arms is red with a yellow diagonal band. A black bear walks along it.
34855.m: There is a yellow stripe in the Bern coat of arms.

34856.q: Apart from white, what colour is the coat of arms of Fribourg?
34856.e: The coat of arms of the canton of Fribourg is black at the top and white at the bottom. So it is not red and white.
34856.m: Fribourg has a black and white coat of arms.

34857.q: Who composed the tune of the Swiss Psalm?
34857.e: The monk Alberich Zwyssig wrote the tune in 1841.
